'''''Pachira glabra''''' ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''Bombacopsis glabra'')<ref name="PlantList"/><ref name="Duarte"/> is a tropical wetland tree in the mallow family, [[Malvaceae]], native to eastern [[Brazil]], where it grows along waterways. It is generally known by the nonscientific names '''Guinea peanut''',<ref name="PBCRC"/><ref name="Duarte"/> '''French peanut''',<ref name="Duarte"/> '''Saba nut''',<ref name="PFAF"/> '''money tree''',<ref name="Duarte"/> and '''lucky tree'''.<ref name="Duarte"/> It shares many of these common names with the similar ''[[Pachira aquatica|P. aquatica]]''.

==Description==
[[File:Castaño (Pachira glabra) (14295858313).jpg|thumb|Flower]]
[[File:Pachira glabra BotGardBln1105LeavesFruitB.jpg|thumb|Foliage]]

''Pachira glabra'' reaches heights of {{convert|9|-|18|m|ft|-1|sp=us}},<ref name="Duarte"/> and its leaves are compound with a fan of 5 to 9 leaflets.<ref name="Duarte"/> It has smooth greenish-gray bark and the trunks are often swollen at the base,<ref name="Duarte"/> even at a young age.<ref name="Hawaiian"/> Its large, white, fragrant flowers bloom on a long, terminal [[peduncle (botany)|peduncle]],<ref name="Duarte"/> opening at night and dropping by the middle of the following day.<ref name="Hawaiian"/> Its {{convert|10|-|20|cm|in|0|adj=mid|-long|sp=us}} smooth green fruit split open naturally to reveal 10 to 25 irregularly rounded brown seeds that are roughly {{convert|2.5|cm|4=1|frac=4|abbr=on}} in diameter.<ref name="Duarte"/>

The Pachira glabra plant has a five-lobed shape of its leaves. Because of this reason, in Chinese Feng Shui, Pachira glabra is thought to represent the 5 elements of feng shui: Wood, fire, earth, water and metal, giving it a unique name called money tree as people believe it can create a harmonious balance of positive energy<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Symbolism and History of Pachira Aquatica (Money Tree) |url=https://www.plantsforallseasons.co.uk/blogs/pachira-care/the-symbolism-and-history-of-pachira-aquatica-money-tree |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=Plants For All Seasons |language=en}}</ref>.

=== Similar species ===
''[[Pachira aquatica]]'' (the Malabar chestnut) is quite similar looking, has similar culinary and ornamental uses, and goes by many of the same common names. ''P. aquatica'' has woody gray bark, while ''P. glabra''s{{'}}s is a smoother greenish-gray,<ref name="Duarte" /> and ''P. aquatica'' will only develop a swollen trunk with age.<ref name="Hawaiian" /> Likewise, the flowers of ''P. aquatica'' feature red-tipped petals and red anthers,<ref name="Duarte" /> whereas the flowers of ''P. glabra'' are all white.<ref name="Duarte" /><ref name="Hawaiian" /> In addition, the ''P. aquatica'' blooms last marginally longer than those of ''P. glabra''.<ref name="Hawaiian" /> ''P. glabra'' capsules (fruits) are green rather than brown like those of ''P. aquatica''. Seed yields of ''P. glabra'' are also lower than those of ''P. aquatica''.<ref name="Duarte" />

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is native to eastern [[Brazil]],<ref name="PBCRC" /> where it grows along rivers and other waterways.<ref name="Duarte" />

The tree is highly adaptable to various soils and flourishes in full sun or partial shade.<ref name="Duarte"/><ref name="PFAF"/> The tree is both drought and flood resistant.<ref name="Duarte"/><ref name="PFAF"/>

==Uses==
===Culinary===
''P. glabra'' is grown in West and Central Africa as a foodcrop. The seeds are rich in oil and contain 16% protein and 40–50% fat.<ref name="PBCRC"/> The seeds taste similar to peanuts<ref name="PBCRC"/> and are typically boiled or roasted,<ref name="PFAF"/> with the roasted seeds sometimes ground to make a hot drink.<ref name="PBCRC"/> The young leaves and flowers are also eaten.<ref name="PBCRC"/>

===Ornamental===
Young ''P. glabra'' trees can easily be grown in flowerpots and survive a range of conditions as long as they remain above freezing temperatures.<ref name="PBCRC"/> They are marketed commercially as ornamentals with several small trees in a single [[flowerpot]], their [[trunk (botany)|trunk]]s [[braid]]ed; specimens are similar in appearance to ''P. aquatica'' and the small ornamentals sold as ''P. aquatica'' are almost all actually ''P. glabra''.<ref name="Hawaiian"/><ref name=":Pangpang Shu"/>{{refn|group=nb|Even in Taiwan, where commercial ornamental cultivation of the "Malabar chestnut" ({{lang|zh|馬拉巴栗}}) began, the plants are usually ''P. glabra'' rather than ''P. aquatica''.<ref name=":Pangpang Shu"/><ref name="HKTree"/>}}
